title: Pounding Grape: the exciting wines of Chris Groenewald, from South Africa
summary: Back in 2014 one of South Africa’s most interesting, and probably quirkiest wine projects was born, a collaboration between Michael
content:
Back in 2014 one of South Africa’s most interesting, and probably quirkiest wine projects was born, a collaboration between Michael Roats and winemaker Ryan Mostert. It was a set of two non-vintage wines called Smiley and Silwervis, and a year later this was supplemented by a Syrah under the Terracura label.

It went on hiatus when the winemaker left, and then came back with Chris Groenewald at the helm, and now there’s a further shift towards a clearer brand identity under Chris’ existing brand, Pounding Grapes.

Smiley has stopped, and the final release was version 7. Chris will continue making Syrah for Michael Roats under the Terracura label with the 2025 and 2026 vintages, but Chris has taken over the winery lease and Pounding Grape will be the name going forwards. So evolution, but the quirkiness and sense of fun remains.

Chris’ approach is natural, but he says, ‘I like making wine wines natural and clean.’ In the winery he has 26 plastic eggs, and all the bottles he uses recycled bottles that have been re-washed by a company in Wellington.

Treve (TR) and I each caught up with him separately to try through the new releases, and they are deeply impressive.

Bringing Back the Joy 2025 Durbanville, South Africa
12% alcohol. This is skin-contact Sauvignon Blanc from a vineyard that looks over Table Mountain, with 7 days on skins, then basket pressed into a 300 litre barrel and a 525 litre plastic egg. Fresh, chalky and nicely aromatic with a hint of mint. Lovely perfume and then some structure in the mouth. 94/100 (JG)

This certified organic Sauvignon Blanc is off vines around 20 years old, rooted in Malmesbury shale. After 7 days on skins, this was basket pressed into a plastic egg and 1 300L neutral barrel, where it rested on gross lees 11 months prior to bottling end December with no fining and very loose filtration. Salty throughout, with crushed stone, apricot pith, mandarin, tangerine, and kisses of white pepper, this energetic white is tight, taut, and with a reverb that draws you back to the glass. 900ish bottles. 12%. The idea and name for this wine started back in 2019 thanks to Lukas van Loggerenberg’s gutsy skin contact SB. Chris didn’t like how SB was traditionally handled in South Africa, and inspired by BB King’s The Thrill is Gone, decided to bring back the joy. 93/100 (TR)

Terracura Chenin Blanc 2025 Swartland, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is from a single vineyard called Sky, planted in 1998, with unirrigated bush vines. Most goes to Mullineux for their granite bottling. It’s higher up on the mountain so the granite is less weathered than on the valley floor. Destemmed, left overnight, pressed the next morning into two eggs. This is pure and linear, very mineral and quite elegant. Concentrated with a nice acid line and good texture and salinity. 95/100 (JG)

Unicorns in the Sky 2025 Swartland, South Africa
Chenin Blanc. 75% Sky vineyard, 25% Kweperfontein (planted 1964). Sky was pressed after one night on skins, while the other part was 6 days on skins. Fermented and aged in plastic eggs. This is textured and powerful, and quite lively, showing appealing pear and peach fruit with real depth and purity. The skin ferment adds some depth and a bit of structure. Lovely fruit expression but also some nice fine-grained structure. This is quite beautiful. 95/100 (JG)

From two vineyards in the Paardeberg, this Chenin Blanc is 25% off Kweperfontein (1964 dryland bush vine on decomposed sandy granites, skin fermented over 6 days), and 75% Sky Vineyard (1998 bush vine dry farmed on granite, on skins overnight before pressing). The Sky portion was native fermented and aged in egg, where the 1964 fruit was native fermented and rested in 300L French barrels. All waited 11 months on full lees, with full MLF prior to bottling. Quince and crystalline lemon lead this weighted, buzzy palate, with a vibrato running long through the humming finish. Very much in youth, this will flesh out with time, while holding onto that acid line. 13%  This was named for the unicorn vineyard of Kweperfontein, farmed by Franziska Wickens, and the name will remain even though Sky vineyard will not be a part of future vintages. 93/100 (TR)

Fairies in the Garden 2025 Swartland, South Africa
This is Semillon Gris from Kweperfontein. Lots of juice versus skins because of big berries, and this sent 7 days on skins. Lovely orange colour. Textured and finely spiced with sour cherry, ripe pear and a touch of cherry. Fine-grained with nice spicy flavours to the fruit, showing lovely balance. 94/100 (JG)

This stunner of a Semillon Gris is from 20ish year old naturally mutated vines, also from Franziska Wickens’ Kweperfontein, and its decomposed granitic sands. After 7 days skin ferment, this was basket pressed into 1 egg and 1 225L barrel. Pouring a hazy glowing orange hue, this streaks tangerine, bergamot, pear skin and green herbs along the sleek palate, with a candied quince note in the core, and a lengthy flake salt finish. Great tension and energy throughout. 12%. This label started as skin fermented Gewürztraminer in 2020. Chris said the ferment smelled exactly like gingerbread (Hansel and Gretel), and along with the otherworldly colour, named it like a fairytale. 92/100 (TR)

Just Leave Me Flowers on my Grave NV Swartland
This Chenin comes in a 500 ml bottle, and it is 65% from 2023 with 3 years under flor, coupled with 35% fresh juice from 2026. Oxidative, appley and tangy with a flor-like nose. Some hints of raisin. Tangy and warm and lively and rich and spicy, this is such a complex wine in a unique style. 94/100 (JG)

This just-released Chenin Blanc under flor is a blend of 65% wine from 2023 (quietly resting in 500L barrel under flor), mixed with 35% 2026 Kweperfontein blended in for freshness. It is unfortified at 15%, with concentration due to evaporation. A fantastically nutty, rancio nose, with golden raisin, almond, orange oil, flake salts, and a slight slick of caramel sweetness. Very complexed, long, and super unique for SA, and best enjoyed over an evening (or two). 400 x 500mL bottles released. Chris’ deathbed wine would certainly be a flor affected wine, and this wine’s name plays with the idea of life sprouting underneath from something that should be dead. 94/100 (TR)

Hard Candy Pinotage 2024 Durbanville, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is from the back end of Durbanville looking towards the Swartland, and it is two 225 litre barrels. Beautiful sweet berry fruit aromatics. Lovely texture and freshness with juicy red cherries and plums. Nice freshness and detail here. Grippy and crunchy and pure, with nice direct fruit. Real energy. 95/100 (JG)

This Pinotage comes from Durbanville, off the same farm as his Syrah and SB, but off the other side of the hill, NW facing, on shale, and 15ish year old vines. The fruit was destemmed, with 15% whole berry (partial carbo) before being pressed into 2 x 228L older barrels, for 14 months. Juicy blackcurrant and black plum lead this pure, fresh, and joyous red, seasoned with dusky florals and cracked peppercorn, and wrapped with long, finely dusty / lightly sticky tannins through an espresso finish. A lovely, fresher style at 13%. The name was inspired by Counting Crows’ song Hard Candy. Chris wanted an unadulterated, innocent, simpler style of Pinotage, like the simpler time of eating these heart shaped candies. 93/100 (TR)

Where the Lines Bend Cabernet Franc 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
11% alcohol. The fruit here comes from the Bottelary Hills (Danie Steytler). The grapes came in cold and wouldn’t start fermenting. It took four days for these destemmed grapes to get going and then they had one gentle punch down a day. After basket pressing they were aged in eggs. Lovely floral aromatics with some chalky notes under the floral cherry fruit. Fresh and vivid with lovely acidity. Pure and primary, this is a lighter expression of Cabernet Franc that’s very Loire-like. So juicy and fine. 94/100 (JG)

This Cabernet Franc comes off Stellenbosch’s Bottelary Hills, and a tiny part of the mighty Kaapzicht vineyard, higher up on the hills with an oceanview and Koffeklip soils. The fruit was destemmed and sat for 3 days in a natural cold soak before ferment kicked off. After 10 days, this was basket pressed into 2 x 525L eggs, and bottled late December (with some CO2 at bottling). Wild blackberry, thorns, perfumed plums are lit with tart and crunchy acidity, and framed with long, lightly sticky tannins, taking this to a pink peppercorn dusted finish. A lovely lighter lens for the grape. 11%. 2026 will be half of the production here due to low yields. The name comes from a Jacob Collier interview talking about music and people, and “all these wiggly people trying to be straight lines. Things get interesting where the lines bend”. Chris believes things get interesting when they’re being drawn outside the boxes, like experimenting with this Cab Franc in Stellies, being a wine as the vineyard wants to be made. 94/100 (TR)

Terracurra Syrah 2025 Durbanville, South Africa
13.2% alcohol. This is 100% whole bunch, from Malmesbury shale soils, looking towards table mountain. A mixture of eggs and 300 litre barrels. Crunchy and bright but fluid and floral, with lovely tannins under the sleek black cherry fruit. So good. 96/100 (JG)

title: The new releases from Radford Dale, including Elgin and Vinum bottlings from 2025
summary: Website: https://www.radforddale.com/ I have been following the wines of Radford Dale with some interest over the last three years. The
content:
Website: https://www.radforddale.com/

I have been following the wines of Radford Dale with some interest over the last three years. The Vinum series represents amazing quality for the price, and then there is the estate range, which continues to morph and perform at the highest level. And the Radford Dale Elgin Estate is really finding its feet: this was the Elgin Ridge property that Brian and Marion Smith established, farming biodynamically, and making some excellent wines. When it came time for them to sell, Radford Dale was a great choice, and they have been taking an already excellent vineyard and moulding it in their preferred direction.

With the 2025 wines that I tried here, I thought they were a real step up. Partly this is evolution; partly this is an excellent vintage.

The big change here has been the arrival of a new winemaker, Petroné Thomas. She joined Radford Dale in 2021, and she was promoted from assistant winemaker to winemaker in 2024. Then following the departure of Jacques de Klerk later in 2024, she took responsibility for the Elgin wines too. Petroné has experience in Burgundy and Beaujolais, and the latter has been very interesting considering the emphasis on Gamay that Radford Dale have.

Tom Prior of Raford Dale gives the following updates:

Elgin Estate

‘The vineyards have really come on. We took our first crop in 2026 of the young vines of Chardonnay and Pinot Noir planted in 2022. A little Gamay also (900 litres), which we plan to bottle and which will see the ‘Antidote’ name return. It’s showing a darker fruit to the Polkadraai vineyard, which is exciting. A Beaujolais clone brought into the nursery is planned for planting soon also.’

‘The Cabernet Franc has been the big surprise story for us at Elgin, but with just 0.4ha in the ground currently. The team have been preparing the two Semillon vineyards to regraft over to Cabernet Franc – the neighbouring Semillon vineyard, also planted in 2016, and the high-density block. The Semillon 2025 is the final release.’

‘For the Pinot Noir, the big focus has been on planting our preferred clone of 115, which formed the base of the past Freedom bottlings (when sourced from a leased vineyard). The plantings inherited from Brian and Marion Smith are predominantly 777.’

‘We also welcomed a beautiful oak fermenter from Klaus Pauscha for harvest 2026, who also manufacture the foudré we have gradually acquired for the Stellenbosch winery. This will help us in refining the Pinot Noir at Elgin, the fermentation temperatures and so on. We’ve worked with plastic tubs to date. Another big upgrade to the cellar has been the cooling, which may allow us to experiment with partial malo on the Chardonnay. The big challenge ahead is to gear the cellar up for red wine production and our use of whole-berries, as the young vines start to ramp up tonnage.’

‘We have also planted Chenin Blanc and there is a cool steep faced and terraced slope we will plant another Chenin Blanc plot on, which we plan to train as a bush vine. The eventual estate range will see varietal bottlings of Chardonnay, Chenin Blanc, Pinot Noir, Gamay and Cabernet Franc.’

Radford Dale Terroir

‘No Frankenstein or Renaissance in 2024. The 2024 crop was lovely but not yielding the directness we look for in these two wines, so the fruit went into the Vinum 24 bottlings. As a result, we have sent on the 2025s. This range used to form some 10 wines in all. The Syrah bottlings were discontinued with last releases of Nudity in 2020 and Stellenbosch Syrah in 2021, as was Black Rock (Swartland) in 2020. The vines sourcing the Chardonnay and Grenache redirected as Vinum bottlings.’

Radford Dale Vinum

 ‘Grenache ’25. This is the last bottling with the inclusion of the older Stellenbosch Mountain block. The younger Helderberg site is really coming on, and we reckon it will make for an interesting wine solo.’

‘Gamay ’25. The vines are now 8 and 7 years old in 2025. Petroné completed a harvest at Chateau de la Chaize in Brouilly in 2024, so there are small refinements in the Vinum ’25 release. We have a young plot on the Helderberg we should take a crop of in 2027. This will be great news as we really cannot make enough of this wine currently.’

‘Pinot Noir ’25. This and the Gamay remain the rarest of the Vinum bottlings, owing to lack of supply. Physically in the Gamay and for the Pinot, as it’s just so difficult to source fruit to produce at this price tier. They are still the highest costing wines to produce, but we are fortunate enough to supplement with the Chenin Blanc, with so much great material to work with there and our largest volume in the range relatively. As a result, we can keep these price aligned.’

Current releases

Radford Dale Estate Freedom Pinot Noir 2025 Elgin, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is textural and elegant. There’s a core of sweet strawberry and cherry fruit with a real smoothness, but there’s also some bright cranberry and a bit of grip bookending the sweet fruit really nicely. Lovely finesse and purity here. A light, elegant style with just a little grunt. Pinot crossed with elegant Nebbiolo in terms of style. Really impressive, and probably the best Elgin Pinot Noir I’ve had. 94/100

Radford Dale Frankenstein Pinotage 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
12.5% alcohol. This isn’t all that Pinotage like, which is not a terrible thing. It’s a sleek, elegant red with black cherry and blackberry fruit, a bit of spicy grunt, and then some herbs and sour cherries on the finish. There’s a lot to like here: flesh, sweet fruit, spicy, some sourness and plenty of elegance. Finishes with a touch of bitterness, reminding us that this is Pinotage, in a subtle way. 93/100

Radford Dale Higher Purpose Cabernet Franc 2025 Elgin, South Africa
13.5% alcohol. Organic. This has beautiful floral aromatics with crushed rock and chalk, giving away its Cabernet Franc identity immediately. It’s so fresh with red cherries and a touch of raspberry. The palate is fresh, elegant, supple and has some crunch to the cherry and raspberry fruit. It’s cool-climate Cabernet Franc that just works so well. Vital, incisive and delicious, with more than a hint of seriousness. This one is worth seeking out. 95/100

Radford Dale Touchstone Chardonnay 2025 Elgin, South Africa
13% alcohol. Beautiful aromatics here with toast, spice, roasted almond, pear and peach. It’s harmonious and refined. The palate shows peach and spice with some bold citrus fruit, covering a wide dynamic range: it’s not pinched and taut, but has plenty of depth, without sacrificing the freshness. Bold and intense, but beautifully integrated flavours: a really serious South African Chardonnay. 94/100

Radford Dale Renaissance Chenin Blanc 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
12.5% alcohol. This has lovely intensity. There’s bright, crystalline citrus fruit, with some spicy mineral intensity and then some honey and nut complexity. So expressive with power combined with elegance, finishing fresh with bright acidity. There’s a touch of the Loire in this wine (freshness and restraint, but also mineral intensity), as well as some South African richness. It’s a really beautiful wine. 95/100

Radford Dale Revelation Semillon 2025 Elgin, South Africa
13% alcohol. Beautifully complex with a lovely hint of green as well as textured citrus fruit and a touch of canteloup melon. This has a touch of grapefruit, and some stony, mineral detail. There’s a hint of cucumber and celery, too. Such lovely harmony, combined with a bit of tension. A really serious wine with beautiful purity and finesse. 94/100

Vinum Pinotage 2025 Coastal Region, South Africa
12% alcohol. This is supple, juicy, bright and also plush. Sweet raspberry and cherry fruit with nice texture to the herb-tinged berry fruits. This is fruity and has lovely approachability, with soft tannins and just a hint of bitterness adding a foil to the sweet fruit. Really fresh and expressive, and such fun, combined with a bit of seriousness. 92/100

Vinum Gamay Noir 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
13% alcohol. Sweet spicy aromatic strawberry fruit on the nose with hints of clay, chalk and warm spiciness. The palate is fresh, supple, rounded but also spicy and quite mineral. Beautiful elegance and tension here, but also some mid-palate richness. This is beautiful. Really impressive. 94/100

Vinum Grenache 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
13.5% alcohol. This is really delicious, with sweet, supple red cherry and red currant fruit, showing some silkiness but also nice texture to the fruit. There’s a bit of structure, but the overall impression is one of real elegance, with a hint of almond and fennel. Massive drinkability here. Just so good. 94/100

Vinum Pinot Noir 2025 Cape Coast, South Africa
12% alcohol. This is supple and delicious with sweet ripe cherry and raspberry fruit, with a bit of cranberry crunch. There’s a finesse to this wine, and an ease, too. It doesn’t seem at all forced. Early picking has worked well here, with just a hint of green that works well with the ripe, supple fruit, and there’s no oak to be found. Just lovely. 93/100

Vinum Chardonnay 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
12.5% alcohol. There’s an innate richness to this wine with peach and ripe pear fruit, as well as some spicy detail. Hints of aniseed and subtle toast in the mix. Really rich and refined with nice detail. This is very good. 93/100

Vinum Chenin Blanc 2025 Stellenbosch, South Africa
12.5% alcohol. This is fruit-driven and textured with pear and green apple fruit, showing some brightness allied to depth. Fruity and expressive with nice weight of fruit. 91/100

Notes from last year’s release

Radford Dale Vinum Chenin Blanc 2024 Stellenbosch, South Africa
12.5% alcohol. This is concentrated and has lots of flavour, but it’s also a fresh wine with a nice salty twist to the lively lemon and pear fruit, as well as a slight touch of baked apple. There’s a really nice fresh, floral, mandarin edge to the nose that’s quite inviting, and it finishes with a nice acid flourish. A brilliantly poised example of Chenin Blanc. 93/100

Radford Dale Vinum Chardonnay 2024 Stellenbosch, South Africa
12% alcohol. This is layered and more complex than you’d expect at this price point, with crystalline citrus fruit as well as some pear and peach. Fresh with nice acidity, but it’s not at all harsh. Lovely textural character with some appley detail adding interest and depth. 93/100

Radford Dale Vinum Grenache 2024 Stellenbosch, South Africa
13.5% alcohol. This is bright, supple and fresh with raspberry and strawberry fruit. It’s juicy, pure and vivid with an appealing green hint to the fruit. Tending towards elegance, but with a bit of grip and nice density of fruit. Very stylish, showing off the elegant, understated side of this variety. 93/100

Radford Dale Vinum Gamay Noir 2024 Stellenbosch, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is bright, juicy and vibrant, with cherry and raspberry fruit. Floral with some nice green notes, showing vitality and intensity. This really captures Gamay well, with vibrant berry fruits plus some appealing greenness, and a juicy brightness. Stony and mineral, too. 93/100

Radford Dale Vinum Pinotage 2024 Coastal Region, South Africa
13.5% alcohol. This is ripe and sweetly fruited with soft strawberry as well as a bit of raspberry crunch here. So textured and interesting with lovely sweet fruit backed up with a bit of spicy framing and some structure. This is delicious and massively drinkable, and doesn’t taste much like Pinotage of old, which is a good thing. 93/100

Radford Dale Vinum Pinot Noir 2024 Cape Coast, South Africa
13% alcohol. This is bright and sweetly fruited with ripe cherries and some red berry notes. There’s a good volume here with a core of sweet fruit. Ripe, rich and quite tasty, with lots of sweet fruit in the mix. 91/100

Radford Dale Renaissance Chenin Blanc 2023 Stellenbosch, South Africa
12.5% alcohol. This is a complex, richly textural expression of Chenin Blanc with pear, apple, peach and apricot notes, but it’s not blowsy. Very expressive with nice weight. Bold, rich fruit on the palate with a wide dynamic range, hitting the rich bass but also with good mid and enough treble. Very fine. 95/100

Radford Dale Touchstone Chardonnay 2024 Elgin, South Africa
12.5% alcohol. Organic. Beautiful aromatics with broad pear and peach fruit as well as some grapefruit and a hint of nice parmesan and salt. The palate shows bitter lemon and pear fruit with a saline twist and some spicy framing. It’s a really expressive wine with lots of fruit and some apple notes accompanying the citrus. Lovely flavour dynamics here. There’s even a hint of tequila. So interesting. 94/100

Radford Dale Revelation Semillon 2024 Elgin, South Africa
12.5% alcohol. Organic. This is so distinctive: it’s bright and fresh with pear and lemon fruit, with nice density and some grapefruit pith. There’s depth but it stays very focused, and the crystalline fruit is supported with really good acidity. There’s a concentration of flavour here as well as freshness and acidity. Lovely wine. 94/100

Radford Dale Frankenstein Pinotage 2023 Stellenbosch, South Africa
12% alcohol. This is a really interesting interpretation of Pinotage. There’s some density to the fruit here, with raspberries and cherries as well as a hint of damson, with some earthy hints, a twist of green, and some grippy structure. There’s a Pinotage-like sweet and sour character, with herbs and ripe sweet fruit, but overall this is quite focused, fruit-driven and deliciousness, with just a hint of sourness and bitterness on the finish. Herbs, cherries, plums and some liquorice notes. 92/100

Radford Dale Higher Purpose Cabernet Franc 2024 Elgin, South Africa
13.5% alcohol. This is really bright, vivid and focused with brisk cherry and raspberry fruit as well as some herbal hints and a fine spiciness, as well as some sweet acidity. There’s a chalky note in the background that’s really appealing, and typical of the variety. This is supple and quite elegant with nice precision. Not a big, heavy wine, but one that shows nice poise. 94/100

Radford Dale Freedom Pinot Noir 2024 Elgin, South Africa
This Pinot is supple and delicately structured with sweet cherry and raspberry fruit with a hint of aniseed and some dried herb notes. It’s tending to elegance and shows nice precision, with a sweet, smooth core of fruit and then a touch of dustiness and a bit of structure. 94/100

title: Unusual grape varieties: a tasting at Shrine to the Vine
summary: I’m a fan of lesser known grape varieties, so this tasting, hosted by Shrine To The Vine Broadway Market’s General
content:
I’m a fan of lesser known grape varieties, so this tasting, hosted by Shrine To The Vine Broadway Market’s General Manager Anna Kielsznia, really appealed. Eight wines from interesting varieties. It was a really good evening. Anna presented these wines brilliantly.

Champagne Olivier Horiot Petit Meslier 2018 France
Just one barrel made of this. Horiot have 7 hectares in the Côtes des Bar, in the south of Champagne, but make their own wine from just 2 of these. Petit Meslier is one of the rare Champagne grapes, and there are just 20 hectares planted in France. It’s a cross between Savagnin and Gouais Blanc. Complex, taut and spicy with lovely intensity and depth. Ripe apple, some baked pastry, some nuts, a touch of honey, and then a bright salty finish. Long and quite serious. 95/100

Sclavos Tsaousi 2024 Kefalonia, Greece
The Sclavos family were ship owners who moved to Russia in 1700, then returned after the revolution and planted 50 hectares of vines in Palli in Kefalonia. They farm biodynamically, and winemaking is pretty natural, with just a small amount of sulfites added at bottling. Tsaousi (sometimes written as Tsaoussi) is a grape variety whose origins are disputed: some say Macedonia, others say North Africa. This wine is all about texture: it’s rounded with lovely pear and white peach fruit. Salty, refined, pure. Beautifully poised, a lovely wine. 94/100

Etienne Courtois Les Cailloux du Paradis Romorantin 2022 Vin de France
Romorantin is only allowed in the Cheverny AOC, but this is not an appellation wine. There are 71 hectares spread among 24 growers. It’s only grown in the Cheverny area, which is in Touraine, south of Blois. Its origin is disputed. Les Cailloux de Paradis is a natural wine producer, started by Etienne’s father Claude in 1992, and this wine has no added sulfites. Wonderful aromatics: floral, grapey and honeyed with some melon and pear. The palate is lively and textured with a stony, mineral edge and some aniseed notes. Lovely acid line. 94/100

Niepoort ‘Ururabo’ Gouveio 2019 Douro, Portugal
This is an oddity: it’s made under flor in sherry casks. Gouveio is a Douro white variety that’s the same as Godello in Spain, and there are just 25 hectares planted. Golden in colour, this is textured and powerful with nice spicy detail and a bit of structure. The flor character is subtle, and this is a beautiful mineral-laced wite with precision and tension. So expressive, and finishing a bit salty. 95/100

Matassa ‘Romanissa’ Lledoner Pelut 2024 Roussillon, France
Also known as ‘hairy Grenache’, Lledoner Pelut has hairs under the leaves, and it is regarded as a separate variety, even though technically it is a clone of Grenache. This is a distinctive, natural expression of this variety with a peppery edge to the bright red cherry, raspberry and cranberry fruit. Pure and linear, but there’s also a bit of tannin on the finish. 94/100

Suertes del Marqués ‘Los Pasitos’ Baboso Negro 2022 Orotava, Tenerife
Tenerife use to make a lot of wine in the past, when ships stopped here and replenished their supplies. The vineyard area contracted, but now there’s somewhat of a revival of interest. Jonaton began making wine at Suertes in 2006 from vineyards his father had bought in the 1980s, with the help of Roberto Santana of Envinate. Now he makes the wines himself and they’ve never been better. Baboso Negro is the same as Portugal’s Alfrocheiro. This is stony and linear and bright with lovely peppery notes as well as black cherries, with some volume, but finishing fresh with a nice sour cherry notes. Purity, energy and balance here, as well as deliciousness. 95/100

Fattoria Ruschi Noceti Pòllera 2021 Tuscany, Italy
Ruschi Noceti is based in Lunigiana, part of Tuscany bordering Liguria. The winery was founded in 1978 and in 1994 they began cooperating with the University of Pisa in preserving rare varieties from the region, which are housed on a 1 hectare plot. Pòllera is an interesting variety with compact bunches of dark graoes. This is so expressive with wild strawberry, cherry and raspberry fruit, with a slightly musky edge to the softly textured palate. There’s poise here, nice acidity and a slight saltiness on the finish. Quite lovely. 94/100

Viúva Gomes Colares Tinto Ramisco 2017 Portugal
Not much Colares left, although this Lisbon-adjacent region once had 18 000 hectares of vines. Now there are just 26 remaining. Famously planted in deep sandy soils, the Ramisco variety makes remarkable, ageworthy wines with solid tannins and good acidity. This example is savoury, taut and has good acidity with some brightness to the black fruits, a hint of Campari, and some sour cherry on the finish. 93/100

title: Minimalist Wines, the exciting South African Syrah-focused winery of Sam Lambson
summary: Website: https://www.minimalistwines.com/ I popped into Flint Wines to meet a South African winemaker that everyone is talking about. Sam Lambson
content:
Website: https://www.minimalistwines.com/

I popped into Flint Wines to meet a South African winemaker that everyone is talking about. Sam Lambson is only 28, but he’s got 9 vintages under his belt with his winery Minimalist Wines, which focuses solely on one variety: Syrah.

It was a 1998 Jamet Côte Rôtie that turned him into a Syrah nut, and he’s of the belief that if there are two varieties that can lead the way for South African wine, they are Chenin Blanc and Syrah.

The first minimalist wine was made in 2018, when he was studying at Stellenbosch. He was just 21. UK wine importer Richard Kelley (now of Dreyfuss Ashby) came and tasted, and loved what he discovered. He bought half the first release, and this endorsement was a great encouragement to Sam.

For many years he was working in other peoples’ cellars, but two years ago moved into his own space, in Cape Town. It’s in Gardens, a gentrifying part of town, and he has a working winery in the city that people can come and visit.

It’s just Syrah here, from some special locations. First we have Cape Agulhas, on the Cape South Coast. Sam describes this cool climate area as a crazy, extreme, rural place with lots of wind. Syrah comes in late here: usually, he’ll start picking at the beginning of March, but it can cross into April.

Then there’s Elgin. They have a vineyard next to Rosie Gunn’s Syrah vineyard (Iona) with Cartreif soils. Elgin is also a cool-climate area, and Syrah only just gets ripe here.

Then there’s the Polkadraii Hills, in Stellenbosch. This is a hot spot for high-quality Syrah in South Africa. In 2024 there was a new parcel in Banghoek that has joined the roster.

Connect the Dots is a blended Syrah that brings all these regions into play. And then there are two single vineyard offerings, from Agulhas and Elgin.

Winemaking is the same for all of them. The grapes are hand-picked into kissies (small crates of 18 kg), stacked in a refrigerated truck, and brought to the winery. They are then unloaded, sorted, and end up in a concrete fermenter. In 2018 and 2019 Sam was 100% whole cluster, then he used a destemmer a bit until 2024, and since 2025 in the new winery he’s back to whole cluster. He doesn’t have a destemmer in the winery.

‘Stems tell part of the vintage story,’ he says. ‘They definitely tame the fruit on the warm Western Cape.’ He adds that while he’s working in the coolest bits of the Western Cape, ‘it’s still not Germany.’ Stems tame the warmth.

He’s a negociant, but also a farmer. Half of his parcels are on a long-term lease and he does the farming.

In the winery, Sam does as little as possible. And this approach extends to the vineyard. ‘We do as little as we possibly can, but if we need to use a fungicide to protect our crop, we will,’ he says. ‘We would love to be in a fully organic regenerative set up, but we are just not there yet. If we need to make amendments, we will.’

The wines are aged in a mix of concrete and used oak, and Sam says he’s favouring unlined concrete. ‘It’s much easier to keep clean that old oak.’ He’s not afraid to use sulfites, because ‘brett in Piemonte and brett in Agulhas taste the same.’ He also says that concrete helps with purity and tension.

Minimalist Connect The Dots Syrah 2023 Western Cape, South Africa
This was a difficult vintage: the one where the N2 was washed away. It was wet and cool so they picked earlier, and the wine has turned out really well. Vivid, juicy and peppery; light and elegant. Harmonious berry and cherry fruits with some silkiness. Very old world in style and showing slight development. 93/100

Minimalist Connect The Dots Syrah 2024 Western Cape, South Africa
Textured and fine with some density and nice peppery spiciness. Textured and fine, and quite salty with nice presence and density. There’s some nervousness to the fruit, which has grainy structure and good acidity. Such a stylish Syrah. 94/100

Minimalist Stars in the Dark Syrah 2025 Cape Agulhas, South Africa
13% alcohol. This vineyard is just 5 km from the sea. Wonderfully aromatic, peppery red fruits nose with real elegance. The palate is fresh with white pepper, juicy red fruits, some oregano and thyme herbiness, and some grippy tannins. This is a beautifully bright, layered, complex expression of Syrah. 95/100

Minimalist No Place Like Home Syrah 2025 Elgin, South Africa
Intense, vivid peppery nose with sleek but brooding black cherry fruit. The palate is concentrated and dense but still has freshness. Brooding blackberry and black cherry fruit with a slight salinity. Grainy, spicy and unfurled with good energy and precision. 95/100

Minimalist No Place Like Home Syrah 2024 Elgin, South Africa
Inviting floral aromatics with sweet cherry fruit. Very polished. So silky, sleek and refined on the palate with real elegance and precision. Fine and pure, this is floral and pepper and very refined. Different in style to 2025. 95/100

title: Bordeaux Claret: the new AOC Bordeaux Claret Controllée is an interesting move, broadening the appeal of Bordeaux reds
summary: Bordeaux has a problem. It’s finding it increasingly hard to sell its cheaper red wines. AOP Bordeaux and Bordeaux Supérieur
content:
Bordeaux has a problem. It’s finding it increasingly hard to sell its cheaper red wines. AOP Bordeaux and Bordeaux Supérieur volumes are down by 50% over the last five years. Producers have suffered from changing tastes (red wine is less popular), tariffs and climate change. Many are uprooting their vineyards.

In response, the region has done something that I think is very clever. It has taken an old name, Claret, and used it to define a new category of Bordeaux reds: lighter, fruitier, more approachable, and suitable for light chilling. With this change, packaging of these wines has also stepped into the modern age.

These are wines suited to modern consumer tastes. The term Claret was previously used by the British trade when it described lighter Bordeaux reds, although some UK merchants still use this term to describe all Bordeaux reds, including some that definitely aren’t in this modern category. They’ll have to begin to retire their use of the word.

The idea is for a new category of wines with lower tannin levels, relatively low in alcohol, and potentially up to 7 g/l of residual sugar. This doesn’t mean the wines are sweet. Most professionals can’t spot up to 4 g/l of residual sugar, and many won’t spot 7 g, and a lot of consumers won’t spot this either. It has the effect of rounding out the palate a bit, and making the tannins less abrasive.

The use of ‘Claret’ in conjunction with Bordeaux debuted with the 2025 vintage, and in the first year 16,500 hl were declared by 40 producers. So this is around 2.2 million bottles

Tannins are limited to a 209-55 IPT (Indice de Polyphénols Totaux, or the Total Polyphenol Index), there is no oak, and the colour is light, at 3 to 15 ICM Intensité Colorante Modifiée or Modified Color Intensity). The wines are designed to be served chilled.

I tried three of these wines and was impressed. I think this is a great initiative.

Sainte Barbe Claretttt 2025 Bordeaux Claret, France
13.5% alcohol. This is fresh, quite juicy, and has a little sweetness that rounds out the palate. Delicious ripe strawberry fruit with some sweet cherry. Low tannin and just a bit of grainy structure around the fringes. This is delicious, sweetly fruited, and softly textured and you could happily drink this from the fridge or with a couple of ice cubes in the glass. A great execution of the Claret idea. 89/100

Papa & Tonton Bordeaux Claret 2025 France
12.5% alcohol. Juicy and fruity with nice grainy structure under the red cherry and strawberry fruit, and then some wet stone minerality and a touch of sweetness on the finish. Massive drinkability, with a touch of seriousness, too. Lots to like about this fruit-driven wine that responds well to chilling. 91/100

Esprit Léger Bordeaux Claret 2025 France
12.5% alcohol. Wet stone edge to the redcurrant and cherry fruit nose, as well as some dried herbs. The palate is fresh, light and tangy with a core of sweetly textured cherry and raspberry fruit, showing a hint of crunchy structure, but also a sour cherry finish that counters the sweet fruit really nicely. A really nice example of this new style. 90/100

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Domaine Saint Amant
summary: Website: https://www.domainesaintamant.com/en/ Domaine Saint Amant is located high up at 600 m, with 32 hectares of vines scattered around the
content:
Website: https://www.domainesaintamant.com/en/

Domaine Saint Amant is located high up at 600 m, with 32 hectares of vines scattered around the village of Suzette. The winery was founded by Jacques Wallut in 1992: he’d previously started a technology business, but had to retire at 65 (company rules). So he bought vines in Suzette, but many of the parcels were in bad condition. He pulled them out and planted what he wanted.

I met with Eloïse Nosworthy (pictured), his granddaughter, who now runs the domaine with her mother. The first vintage of Amant was 1995, and her mother became involved in 1996, when she returned from the USA with her English investment banker husband.

Eloïse had decided she’d never be involved, and was working in corporate communications and jewelry making in London. When Covid arrived in 2020, she moved to France and got stuck in with the vintage that year.

They have 6 hectares of white vines, of which 95% are Viognier, a speciality of theirs.

Domaine Saint Amant Barry Viognier 2024 Côtes du Rhône Blanc, France
This is 95% Viognier and 5% Roussanne from 600 m altitude. Textural and fresh with nice brightness. Light and expressive with a hint of pear and apricot. Very expressive for a Viognier. 93/100

Domaine Saint Amant Carlina 2024 Côtes du Rhône Blanc, France
Clairette, Roussanne and Grenache Blanc from Beaumes-de-Venise, at altitude. Juicy, textural, grainy and crystalline with nice freshness, as well as a slight saltiness. Nice presence to this wine. 94/100

Domaine Saint Amant Grangeneuve Beaumes de Venise 2021
14.5% alcohol. This comes from 500 m, and it’s a blend of Grenache, Syrah, Carignan and Viognier. Lively and fresh with some sweet berry fruits as well as wet stone minerality and wild herbs and pepper. Beginning to develop and mellow a little, this is getting a little wild in a good way. 92/100

Domaine Saint Amant Cuvée Nathalie Syrah 2020
14.5% alcohol. 95% Syrah, 5% Viognier. This is sweetly aromatic with apricot, cherry and pepper notes, and then some warm, sweet, stewed strawberry on the palate. Softening and losing definition with age, it’s very appealing but I suspect it would have been a bit brighter and more focused younger. 91/100

Domaine Saint Amant Bonelli Beaumes de Venise 2024
14% alcohol. Organic. 80% Grenache, 20% Syrah. Juicy, vivid, supple cherry and raspberry fruit with some nice herbal hints. There’s a massive drinkability and freshness to this wine which has a lovely hint of wildness, while staying fully correct! This is really good. 94/100

BEAUMES-DE-VENISE

  • Xavier Vignon

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: a big tasting of the reds and the Muscats
summary: This was a great chance to look at a wide range of wines from this cru, beginning with the red
content:
This was a great chance to look at a wide range of wines from this cru, beginning with the red wines and then going on to the Muscats.

Bonpas Grand Cardinal Beaumes de Venise 2024
14.5% alcohol. Supple, sweetly aromatic nose with cherries and raspberries. The palate is bright with some peppery framing and nice vivid acidity keeping things fresh. A juicy, slightly tart, lighter style that has a lot of drinkability. 90/100

Château La Croix des Pins Les Contreforts de Montmirail Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. Organic, single vineyard. This has some pepper and herb complexity as well as ripe, slightly heady cherry and plum fruit. There’s quite a bit of spicy complexity here, bringing a savoury dimension to the sweet fruit. 92/100

Demoiselle Suzette Rouge Désir Beaumes de Venise 2024
14% alcohol. Nice concentration here with bold, sweet cherry and berry fruits with some spicy definition. Has some grippy tannin in the mix. Stylish and well balanced with nice intensity. 93/100

Domaine de Cassan Le Coeur des Dentelles Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. 90% Grenache, 10% Syrah. This is really bright, fresh and peppery with nice mineral notes interleaving among the sweet, focused cherry and berry fruits. This has good definition and plenty of drinkability, despite the relatively high alcohol. 93/100

Domaine des Bernadins Beaumes de Venise 2024
14% alcohol. A blend of 60% Grenache, 25% Syrah, 6% Marsanne, 5% Mourvèdre, 4% Grenache Blanc. Warmly aromatic with lovely pepper and herb complexity as well as ripe cherry fruit. The palate is fresh and complex with pepper, meat, herbs and sleek cherry and berry fruits. Real focus, depth and complexity here. 95/100

Domaine des Garances Alzard Beaumes de Venise 2024
14.5% alcohol. Organic. 65% Grenache, 35% Syrah. Beautifully expressive nose with a fine peppery edge to the sweet berry fruits. The palate is elegant and expressive with nice dusty tannins providing a backbone, and a sense of freshness to the fruit. Juicy and expressive, this is really good. 94/100

(Elizbeth & Philippe Bernard) Domaine La Ligière Les Garennes Beaumes de Venise 2024
14% alcohol. Organic. 60% Grenache, 40% Syrah. Slight meaty nose with some char notes, as well as bright berry fruits. The palate is vivid and substantial with rich berry and cherry fruit, with a spicy, structured finish. Rich style. 92/100

Domaine Raboly Clément V Beaumes de Venise 2024
14% alcohol. 1.5 hectares, 6000 vines, 8 tonnes of grapes. 70% Grenache and 30% Syrah. Massal selection, raised in ancient barrels previously used for Muscat. This is nicely dense but also well balanced with a core of sweet blackberry and cherry fruit, with a slight saltiness and lovely peppery detail. Concentrated but refined with nice intensity and balance. 94/100

Domaine Saint Amant Bonelli Beaumes de Venise 2024
14% alcohol. Organic. 80% Grenache, 20% Syrah. Juicy, vivid, supple cherry and raspberry fruit with some nice herbal hints. There’s a massive drinkability and freshness to this wine which has a lovely hint of wildness, while staying fully correct! This is really good. 94/100

Domaine Saint Roch Epyminia Beaumes de Venise 2024
14.5% alcohol. 90% Syrah, 10% Viognier. This is really good. It has a floral nose with a touch of apricot, some white pepper, and lovely black cherry fruit. The palate has a bit of grippy structure, but also lovely fresh fruit. So expressive and well balanced, with warmth but also definition. 95/100

Domaine Pierre Rougon Beaumes de Venise 2024
15.5% alcohol. 70% Grenache, 25% Syrah, 5% Viognier. Aromatic black fruits nose with a peppery, herby edge. Alluring and rich. The palate is rich and full with juicy, layered, textured fruit. Nice depth to this rich wine. 92/100

Martinelle Beaumes de Venise 2024
14.5% alcohol. Organic. 60% Grenache, 40% Syrah. This is fresh and vivid with appealing sweet black cherry and blackberry fruit, showing nice definition and finishing with a spicy flourish. Has some tannin. 92/100

Rhonea Confidence Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. Half/half Grenache and Syrah. Juicy and sweetly aromatic with nice depth to the liquorice-laced berry and cherry fruit. Ripe but still in balance with a touch of warmth on the finish. Stylish. 92/100

Domaine Caroline Bonnefoy Beaumes de Venise 2023
14% alcohol. 75% Grenache, 25% Syrah. Organic. Really lively herb-laced, peppery raspberry fruit on the nose. The palate is peppery and herby with juicy cherry and berry fruits, and then a lovely dried herb and pepper savouriness. Fresh and expressive, and with massive drinkability. 94/100

Domaine de Fenouillet Terres Blanches Beaumes de Venise 2023
14.5% alcohol. Organic. 50% Grenache, 35% Syrah, 15% Mourvèdre. Bright and with nice energy, but also some meaty, spicy depth. Shows sweet cherry and berry fruit with nice intensity and a bit of grip on the finish. Lots of presence here. 93/100

Domaine de la Ferme Saint-Martin ‘Saint-Martin’ Beaumes de Venise 2023
14.5% alcohol. 95% Grenache, 5% Syrah, organic. Peppery, herby and spicy with some char and liquorice notes on the nose. The palate is meaty and spicy with a savoury twist to the bright berry fruits. Lovely detail to this wine: it’s quite intriguing. 93/100

Domaine de la Ferme Saint-Martin Les Terres Jaunes Beaumes de Venise 2023
13% alcohol. 70% Grenache, 20% Syrah, 5% Teret Noir, 5% Counoise. Organic. Complex, open, herby, peppery nose with some juicy red fruits. The palate is bright and expressive with lots of energy, bright cherry fruit, a touch of cranberry, and massive drinkability. This is quite lovely. A real outlier, but delicious and thought-provoking. 95/100

Domaine de Piéblanc Les Hauts Beaumes de Venise 2023
14.5% alcohol. Organic. From 300 m at the foot of Mont Ventoux, this is a blend of equal parts Syrah and Grenache. Juicy, peppery and a bit meaty, this shows ripe but well defined cherry and plum fruit with a touch of warmth, but always staying balanced and appealing. Slightly meaty on the finish. 93/100

Domaine des Garances Le Jas du Chene Beaumes de Venise 2023
14% alcohol. Organic. 50% Grenache, 50% Syrah. Rich, vivid, juicy and spicy with a subtle cured meat edge to the lush blackberry and cherry fruit. Nice definition to this wine, with some structure and spice on the finish. 93/100

Domaine Les Goubert Beaumes de Venise 2023
14.5% alcohol. Grenache, Syrah and Cinsault, organically farmed. Leather, herbs and spice on the nose, as well as bright, ripe berry fruits. The palate is intriguing, with brightness and a sense of lightness, but also some rich, sweet fruit. There’s a herbal twist and even a touch of mint. The Cinsault seems to be delivering something here in terms of lightness and texture, but also the fruit profile. Beautiful. 95/100

Domaine Raboly Clément V Beaumes de Venise 2023
14% alcohol. 70% Grenache, 30% Syrah. Juicy and bright with fresh redcurrant and red cherries, framed by some dried herbs and pepper. There’s a lovely focus and elegance to this wine, which has juiciness and drinkability as well as a bit of complexity. Not heavy. 94/100

Domaine Raboly Jean XXII Beaumes de Venise 2023
14% alcohol. 70% Syrah, 30% Grenache. This is bright, expressive and peppery with lovely black cherry and blackberry fruit, combining a core of sweet, ripe fruit with some nice grippy structure, finishing fresh. Great balance here. 94/100

Famille Manganelli René Beaumes de Venise 2023
15% alcohol. Old vines on the yellow marnes of Trias. Organic. Ripe, sweet fruit here with some pepper and herbs alongside rich, dense, sweet berry and cherry fruit. Long, warm finish. Lovely concentration and balance to this wine. 94/100

Rhonea Trias Beaumes de Venise 2023
15% alcohol. From Trias: gypsum and red clay soils at 300 m. Lovely aromatics of pepper-laden cherry fruits. Nice weight on the palate, which is rich and concentrated but well balanced with lovely sweet cherry and berry fruit. Quite textured. A bit of warmth on the finish, but overall really good – and it’s great to see the soils taking centre stage. 94/100

Rhonea La Beaume Beaumes de Venise 2023
14.5% alcohol. Grey Jurassic clays. Rich, sweetly fruited, spicy and peppery on the nose. Enticing. The palate is very bold with some chocolate, herbs, meat and spice as well as dense cherry and berry fruits. Forward and enticing, with some structure, too. 93/100

Desmoiselle Suzette Rouge Désir 2022
14.5% alcohol. Supple, light, and warmly fruited with some dried herbs as well as sweet red cherry fruit. Nice definition here. This has an ease to it, and it’s very drinkable. 92/100

Domaine de Durban Vieilles Vignes Beaumes de Venise 2022
14.5% alcohol. 75% Grenache, 20% Syrah, 5% Mourvèdre. This is warm, spicy and fruity, with a nice combination of sweet berry fruits, some floral cherry and herb detail, and a bit of grainy structure. Drinking very well now, this is a warmly satisfying red wine. 92/100

Domaine La Ferme Saint-Martin Diapir Beaumes de Venise 2022
13% alcohol. 50% Grenache, 25% Syrah, 15% Teret Noir, 10% Counoise. Expressive, vivid, very spicy and very peppery with bright wild strawberry and cherry fruit with nice herbal hints and good structure and acidity. This is a brilliantly expressive wine that has massive drinkability, plus some seriousness, too. 94/100

Domaine La Ferme Saint-Martin Costancia Beaumes de Venise 2022
13% alcohol. 50% Syrah, 50% Grenache Noir. Lively, peppery, herbal and bright with nice energy to the slightly compressed cherry and berry fruits. This is a lovely wine made in a slightly earlier-picked style and it works so well, with juicy fruit but also layers of detail and flavour. So interesting. 94/100

Domaine des Garances Pierre Beaumes de Venise 2022
14.5% alcohol. 50% Carignan, 25% Grenache, 25% Syrah. Organic. Juicy, vivid and bright with red cherry and redcurrant fruit and some nice structure. There’s a great energy to this wine, with the Carignan bringing freshness and the Syrah and Grenache filling in the holes. Really lovely. 94/100

Domaine Raboly Beaumes de Venise 2022
15% alcohol. 70% Syrah, 30% Grenache. There’s a lovely ripe fruit quality to the nose, which shows sweet cherries. The palate is rounded and sweetly fruited, with some nice peppery hints and also a touch of bitterness from the alcohol. But this is drinking very nicely now. 93/100

Domaine St Roch Cuvée Mes Sens Beaumes de Venise 2022
15% alcohol. 60% Syrah, 40% Grenache. Rich and ripe with slightly stewed fruit, some herbal hints, and then some warmth on the finish. This is a bit herbal. 89/100

Domaine St Roch Cuvée des Taus Beaumes de Venise 2022
14.5% alcohol. 60% Grenache, 30% Syrah, 10% Cinsault. Delightfully peppery and expressive with some strawberry and cherry fruit, a bit of sweetness to the palate, and a sense of elegance and drinkability. I think the Cinsault has had a very positive influence on this blend. Quite lovely. 94/100

Famille Manganelli René Beaumes de Venise 2022
15% alcohol. Trias terroir, organically farmed. Supple and fruity with a nice brightness to the cherry, plum and strawberry fruit. There’s a bit of herbal detail, too. Shows warmth and yet stays drinkable – a really nice wine. 93/100

La Pigeade Beaumes de Venise 2022
14% alcohol. This is well balanced with notes of wild herbs, white pepper and red cherries. Textural and spice-laden, it’s beginning to open out into a mellow place. Stylish and well balanced. 93/100

Gabriel Meffre Laurus Beaumes de Venise 2022
15% alcohol. This is ripe, open and herby with a core of sweet berry fruit as well as some grippy structure at the fringes. Ripe and enticing with nice depth of fruit. 90/100

Xavier Vignon Beaumes de Venise 2022
15% alcohol. Juicy, herby and supple with a sweet, elegant core of strawberry and cherry fruit. Warming and well balanced, this has an ease about it. 92/100

Domaine de Piéblanc Serre de Supion Beaumes de Venise 2021
15% alcohol. 300m altitude, matured in 450 litre barrels. Warm, spicy and quite mature on the nose with a hint of Christmas cake. Rich and ripe on the palate with some mellow maturity, showing a slightly baked edge to the fruit. 89/100

Domaine des Garances Le Pas de L’Aube Beaumes de Venise 2021
14.5% alcohol. 75% Syrah, 25% Grenache. Organic. The fruit has receded a bit but there’s nice structure here, with a hint of mint and spice as well as compact berry fruits. Grippy and tannic on the finish. There’s substance here. 91/100

Domaine Saint Amant Grangeneuve Beaumes de Venise 2021
14.5% alcohol. This comes from 500 m, and it’s a blend of Grenache, Syrah, Carignan and Viognier. Lively and fresh with some sweet berry fruits as well as wet stone minerality and wild herbs and pepper. Beginning to develop and mellow a little, this is getting a little wild in a good way. 92/100

Domaine Saint Amant Cuvée Nathalie Syrah 2020
14.5% alcohol. 95% Syrah, 5% Viognier. This is sweetly aromatic with apricot, cherry and pepper notes, and then some warm, sweet, stewed strawberry on the palate. Softening and losing definition with age, it’s very appealing but I suspect it would have been a bit brighter and more focused younger. 91/100

Xavier Vignon Arcane L’Etoile Beaumes de Venise NV
15% alcohol. No vintage declared on this wine. Elegant and slightly peppery with layered cherry, strawberry and plum fruit. Rounded, with a bit of spicy framing and some silkiness, but also a bit of structure on the finish. Very stylish and quite intriguing. 93/100

Domaine Pierre Rougon Hommage Beaumes de Venise 2020
15.5% alcohol. Warm, sweetly fruited and quite dense, with a wall of ripe cherries and plums. Beginning to mellow and broaden, showing nice depth and intensity. Hints of pepper and mint on the finish. 91/100

Muscat

Domaine Fontavin Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Week-end à Venise 2025
15.5% alcohol. Muscat Blanc à Petit Grains. Organic. This is really pleasant, grapey and rounded with a nice bitter twist on the finish. Sweet and pure with a touch of barley sugar. 90/100

Domaine St Roch Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Cuvée Amour 2025
15% alcohol. Fresh, bright and tangy with mandarin and table grape notes. Sweet and enticing, but stays bright and quite light in weight. 92/100

Famille Manganelli Muscat de Beaumes de Venise ‘Alain’ 2025
15% alcohol. Organic. Fruity and expressive with a touch of grapefruit and herb alongside the sweet grapey notes. There’s a detailed spiciness here that’s very attractive. Has a touch of sake about it. 93/100

Lumian Bonnefoy Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. Organic. Oxidative appley edge to the grapey nose. The palate is sweet but fresh with apples and herbs, as well as some spiciness. I’m not keen on the oxidative characters here. 85/100

La Pigeade Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. Fruity and grapey with a slight appley edge to the sweet fruit. Has a sense of freshness and then a bitter tang on the finish. 89/100

Domaine des Bernardins Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. 25% red Muscat in the blend, giving a bit of colour. This is rich and complex with layered table grape and canteloup melon notes, as well as some tinned pear and a hint of tea. Lovely depth and complexity here. 94/100

La Ligière Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
Fresh and fruit-driven with a touch of spiciness as well as sweet table grape and pear fruit. Nice purity and concentration here, and finishes bright and fresh. Lovely. 93/100

Domaine Pierre Rougon Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. There’s some depth and complexity here with sweet table grape and melon, as well as orange peel and aniseed notes. Broad and lovely with good intensity. 93/100

Rhonea Carte Or Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15.5% alcohol. Fresh, minty and fruity on the nose. Lively palate is sweet and textured with nice weight and a good balanced. Finishes warm and spicy, but also quite fresh. 92/100

Xavier Vignon Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15% alcohol. Nice depth here with some layers of spice interweaving with the textured pear and grape notes. Rich but in balance, finishing sweet. 92/100

Desmoiselle Suzette Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2023
15% alcohol. Fresh, rounded and fruity with some barley sugar and table grape notes. Fruity and expressive and quite stylish. 91/100

Domaine de Durban Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2023
15% alcohol. Nicely expressive with a lovely fruity quality. Hints of aniseed with ripe table grapes and some ripe melon, finishing warm and sweet. 91/100

Adrien Roustan Domaine D’Ouréa Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2023
15% alcohol. Organic. Ripe and rich with a slight nutty undercurrent to the sweet pear and table grape fruit. Has some depth and substance, with a fine spicy finish. Freshness and depth here. 93/100

Domaine du Fenouillet Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Sélection Ancestrale 2023
15% alcohol. 10% red Muscat. Full golden colour. Complex, spicy and layered with lovely depth, a hint of structure, and nice apple, pear and table grape characters. Good concentration and depth here, showing real interest. 94/100

Domaine Les Ondines Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2019
15% alcohol. Full golden colour. Lively, spicy and complex on the nose with some marmalade and spice. Honeyed and appley on the palate with nice development and some complexity. 93/100

Domaine St Roch Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Plaisir 2025
15.5% alcohol. This is 50/50 Blanc and Rouge, and it’s very pale pink in colour. Lively, bright and sweet with some grapefruit and pineapple, finishing fresh. 91/100

Vignoble Alain Ignace Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Le Petit Grain d’Antonin 2025
15% alcohol. Organic. A blend of Blanc and Rouge, pale pink in colour. Juicy, fruity, bright and energetic with mandarin and sweet melon notes, finishing bright. Very fruity and appealing. 91/100

Famille Manganelli Muscat de Beaumes de Venise ‘Émilie’ 2025
15% alcohol. Organic. Made from Muscat Rouge. Pale red in colour, this is fresh, bright and fruity with an appley edge to the table grape fruit, and then just a hint of red cherry. Finishes bright. Really appealing: sweet and enticing. 93/100

Desmoiselle Suzette Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Rouge Plaisir 2024
15% alcohol. Red Muscat. Quite a full red colour. Juicy, tart, bright and energetic. Sweet pear, table grape and cherry fruit. Has a bit of structure, too, countering the primary fruit, and finishes juicy and tart. Really lovely. 94/100

Domaine St. Roch Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Cuvée Désir 2024
15.5% alcohol. Muscat rouge. Light red in colour. Fresh, juicy and quite lovely with strawberries, table grapes and tart cherries, combining sweetness with freshness. Really delightful, and very pure and fine. 93/100

Vignoble Alain Ignace Muscat de Beaumes de Venise ‘La Péché d’Émilie’ 2024
15% alcohol. Organic. Red muscat. Deeply coloured. Lively and spicy with nice depth to the cherry and raspberry fruit, with some grapey sweetness. Has lovely fruit and also some structure. 93/100

Rhonea Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Bois Doré Age 6 Years
15% alcohol. Full golden colour. Aged in a new barrel, this is very woody and spicy, with a minty, cedary edge to the sweet fruit. It’s an unusual take on Beaumes de Venise, and I’m not sure about it: the wood really dominates. But some might really love this style! 88/100

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Rhonea
summary: I met with Fabien Cabezas and Sophie Steinloff to explore the wines of Rhonea, a cooperative. Fabien has 112 hectares
content:
I met with Fabien Cabezas and Sophie Steinloff to explore the wines of Rhonea, a cooperative. Fabien has 112 hectares that he farms with his brother, and he provides the coop with 16 hectares of vines. Sophie (who works for Rhonea) explains that the coop is open to the new generation of growers, and allows them to do their own wines as well as sell to the coop.

Rhonea is a union of wine producers who have the option of doing Rhonea brands, or they can make single estate wines, too. The winegrowers get a ranking based on quality, which the cooperative is keen on fostering.

It’s based in Beaumes-de-Venise, but they also make Vacqueyras, Ventoux and Gigondas, from 1300 hectares of vines owned by 142 families. They make half of the Beaumes-de-Venise wines, and 60% of the Muscats.

I was really impressed with the work they are doing here.

Rhonea Confidence Beaumes de Venise 2023 France
14.5% alcohol. Grenache and Syrah raised in used oak. This is fresh and supple with sweet raspberry and cherry fruit. Floral and expressive with a slight saltiness. This has lovely purity of fruit with nice texture. Quite lovely. 94/100

Rhonea Confidence Beaumes de Venise 2024 France
15% alcohol. Half/half Grenache and Syrah. Juicy and sweetly aromatic with nice depth to the liquorice-laced berry and cherry fruit. Ripe but still in balance with a touch of warmth on the finish. Stylish. 92/100

Rhonea Trias Beaumes de Venise 2023 France
15% alcohol. From Trias: gypsum and red clay soils at 300 m, that become very hard like concrete. Lovely aromatics of pepper-laden cherry fruits. Nice weight on the palate, which is rich and concentrated but well balanced with lovely sweet cherry and berry fruit. Quite textured. A bit of warmth on the finish, but overall really good – and it’s great to see the soils taking centre stage. 94/100

Rhonea La Beaume Beaumes de Venise 2023
14.5% alcohol. Grey Jurassic clays. Rich, sweetly fruited, spicy and peppery on the nose. Enticing. The palate is very bold with some chocolate, herbs, meat and spice as well as dense cherry and berry fruits. Forward and enticing, with some structure, too. 93/100

Rhonea Carte Or Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2024
15.5% alcohol. Fresh, minty and fruity on the nose. Lively palate is sweet and textured with nice weight and a good balanced. Finishes warm and spicy, but also quite fresh. 92/100

Rhonea Muscat de Beaumes de Venise Bois Doré Age 6 Years
15% alcohol. Full golden colour. Aged in a new barrel, this is very woody and spicy, with a minty, cedary edge to the sweet fruit. It’s an unusual take on Beaumes de Venise, and I’m not sure about it: the wood really dominates. But some might really love this style! 88/100

title: Beaumes-de-Venise exploration: Domaine du Durban
summary: Gaetan Leydier hosted us at Domaine de Durban, a significant producer in the region with 70 hectares of vines, of
content:
Gaetan Leydier hosted us at Domaine de Durban, a significant producer in the region with 70 hectares of vines, of which 56 hectares are around the winery. This sort of concentration of vineyard holdings is quite rare in the region. We also bumped into Gaeten’s father, Henri.

This is a family domaine that was taken over by his great grandparents in 1967. They have 30 hectares in red Beaumes-de-Venise, 20 hectares of Muscat, and then 6 hectares in Gigondas, which is next door.

The two sides of the estate are at different levels, with different expositions. They have mostly clay soils, but there’s also quite a bit of trias here.

Domaine de Durban Vieilles Vignes Beaumes de Venise 2022
14.5% alcohol. 75% Grenache, 20% Syrah, 5% Mourvèdre. This is warm, spicy and fruity, with a nice combination of sweet berry fruits, some floral cherry and herb detail, and a bit of grainy structure. Drinking very well now, this is a warmly satisfying red wine. 92/100

Domaine de Durban Beaumes de Venise Cuvée Prestige 2022
14.5% alcohol. 70% Grenache (from trias terroir), 25% Syrah, 5% Mourvèdre. Old, large wooden casks. Warm, spicy nose with a slight pepperiness. This is vibrant and juicy on the palate but also has some depth, with nice concentration and a drying tannic structure that works well as a foil to the sweet fruit. Very stylish with good balance. 94/100

Domaine de Durban Beaumes de Venise Esprit de Famille 2020
Plot selection of old vines, with some of the vines 130 years old. 65% Grenache, 30% Syrah, 5% Mourvèdre. Warm, spicy nose with some oak evident. The palate is structured and dense with some brightness, but also depth. The oak is very high up in the mix in this wine, taking it in a bit of a different direction. 91/00

Domaine de Durban Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 2023
15% alcohol. Nicely expressive with a lovely fruity quality. Hints of aniseed with ripe table grapes and some ripe melon, finishing warm and sweet. 91/100

Domaine de Durban Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 1999
Golden colour. Spice, mint and honey on the nose with tinned pear, peach and table grape notes. The palate is sweet and spicy with a distinct minty edge with marmalade, melon and then some warm spiciness on the finish. Honeyed and slightly waxy with lovely depth. Mellow and enticing. 94/100

Domaine de Durban Muscat de Beaumes de Venise 1990
Lovely mint and spice nose with real intensity. Notes of honey, mint and spice. Still fresh with real complexity and some subtle savoury notes. Delicious. 95/100
